ai.en: The Saturday Farmers' Market in the redeveloped North Building of St. Lawrence Market, with seasonal produce, baked goods, meat, cheese and flowers.

events.description: Visit the Saturday Farmers' Market in the newly redeveloped St. Lawrence Market North building. Discover seasonal produce, baked goods, meats, cheeses, flowers and pantry staples from local vendors all under one roof.

title.en: The Stop Farmers' Market @ Wychwood Barns Park

ai.en: The Stop Farmers' Market at Wychwood Barns Park, with more than 35 weekly vendors and a focus on healthy food access.

events.description: Featuring 35+ weekly vendors, the market brings together local farmers, food producers, and neighbours to increase access to healthy food in ways that build community. A program of The Stop Community Food Centre, the market supports both emerging and established small-scale producers while strengthening a resilient local food economy through responsibly grown and produced food. The market is committed to affordability, supporting racialized vendors, and creating welcoming, community-driven public spaces. Reflecting the diverse cultures of the neighbourhood and the broader GTA, the market celebrates the many food traditions that make Toronto vibrant. Come visit and support our year-round community market operating every Saturday in the Bathurst–St. Clair neighbourhood.

ai.en: The Beach Photo Club Exhibition at the Clark Centre for the Arts, photographs from realistic to abstract.

events.description: Enjoy this photography exhibition by a diverse group of artists as they present their unique interpretations of our world, from realistic to abstract, including techniques such as macro photography, intentional movement and digital compositing. This collection promises a rich visual experience that reflects the wide-ranging creativity of Beach Photo Club members.

ai.en: Patterns That Aren't, an exhibition at Cedar Ridge Creative Centre by David Currie on how people seek out patterns to adapt to their surroundings.

events.description: Step into the intricate world of artist David Currie as he explores how humans are hard-wired to seek out patterns as a means of adapting to their environment, whether connecting imaginary lines to stars or writing algorithms that direct a robot’s movements. But once a pattern is understood, interest tends to fade. Here, Currie has developed a refreshingly new visual vocabulary, one built to engage rather than fade into the background in his series of large-scale, mixed media, papercut artworks that combine recent discoveries in mathematics with a lifetime of the artist’s skill, development and commitment.

title.en: Saturday Farmers Market at Evergreen Brick Works

events.description: Discover Toronto’s largest farmers market, happening year-round every Saturday at Evergreen Brick Works! Shop fresh, seasonal produce, artisanal goods, and locally prepared foods from Ontario farmers and small businesses. Looking for the perfect winter weekend? Stroll through our indoor market filled with delicious food and one-of-a-kind finds, sip on a cozy hot chocolate or coffee, and discover the history of the old brick factory on our free guided tours. Wrap it up with a peaceful walk on the outdoor trails or enjoy our ice rink—your winter escape, all in one place! By supporting the farmers market, you’re helping to sustain local agriculture and small businesses. Bring your friends, family, and reusable bags for a fun shopping experience! Getting there is easy with the free shuttle bus picking up next to Broadview Station or take the TTC's 28 bus from Davisville Station.
events.address: 550 Bayview Ave, East York, ON, M4W 3X8

events.description: Start your adventure at our launch pad, where you’ll receive a boarding pass before stepping aboard Santa's spaceship equipped with 360-degree screens and surround sound. Prepare for a magical journey through space, arriving at the North Pole in Santa’s control room! Capture the moment with a keepsake 5x7 photo included. Hours of Operation: November 12 – December 23 | 9 AM – 9 PM December 24 | 9 AM – 3 PM Each reservation is 5 minutes with multiple bookings per timeslot. Each reservation can accommodate up to 5 family members. Due to popular demand, flight pins will be available for purchase onsite, while supplies last. NEW: Pre-purchase valet for $15 with your ticket, conveniently located in Parkade E by Simons, or $20 when purchased onsite. A Note to Our Guests: We’re excited to make your Journey to the North Pole a truly magical and memorable experience! This attraction includes lighting effects, surround sound, and other sensory elements some guests may be sensitive to. Guests have the option to forego the immersive experience and visit Santa only. For a full list of Frequently Asked Questions, visit yorkdale.com.

ai.en: SignFest Toronto 2026 at North York Memorial Community Hall, a free festival of Deaf culture, sign language and accessibility, with a daytime expo.

events.description: This is a free public festival celebrating Deaf culture, sign language, accessibility, and inclusion. The festival features a free daytime expo with vendors, exhibitors, organizations, presentations, entertainment, and networking opportunities. In the evening, internationally acclaimed Deaf rapper and performer SignMark from Finland will perform his Final Canada Tour – "One Last Time." Join us for a full day of connection, learning, and celebration in Toronto.
events.address: 5110 Yonge Street North York, ON M2N 5V7

ai.en: The 74th Open Juried Exhibit at the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery, where Colour and Form Society members and non-members show work.

events.description: Colour and Form Society presents an exhibit opportunity for their artists to showcase a myriad of talent, and for non-members to be juried into membership of the organization. The Colour and Form Society was established in 1952 and has played a significant role in the cultural mosaic of Canada—promoting diversity, creative freedom, and independence in art. Reception: November 1, 2–4 p.m.
events.address: 399 The West Mall, Etobicoke, ON, M9C 2Y2

ai.en: The Allan Gardens Saturday Farmers' Market at the Children's Conservatory, with fresh produce and small-scale producers.

events.description: Celebrate local food, community, and sustainable agriculture. Discover fresh produce, artisanal products, and small-scale producers - all while connecting with the people who grow and create them.We invite you to come meet the vendors, discover new favourites, and taste the heart of your community! The Allan Gardens Farmers’ Market facilitates a direct exchange between local farmers, food producers, artisan makers, and consumers. Everything sold at the market (50%+1) must be grown, sourced, made, and/or prepared in Toronto and the surrounding area—ensuring that every purchase supports your neighbourhood economy. Join us year- round every Saturday from 10am-2pm, in the beautiful Allan Gardens Children’s Conservatory & Teaching Garden.

ai.en: The Sunday Variety Market at St. Lawrence Market's Big White Tent, now open every Saturday and Sunday as a weekend treasure hunt.

events.description: Get ready for the ultimate weekend treasure hunt! The Sunday Variety Market is now open every Saturday and Sunday, bringing the city’s biggest and most exciting market experience to life each week. Discover over 75 incredible vendors—dive into vintage fashion from every era, luxury finds, one-of-a-kind handmade goods, unique gifts, antiques, collectibles, sparkling jewelry, and local gems you won’t find anywhere else. Shop vintage like a true Toronto insider under the iconic big white tent and experience the city’s most vibrant small business community in the heart of downtown! If you’re looking for weekend plans in Toronto, don't miss this free event St. Lawrence Market - Toronto's most historic cultural destination.

ai.en: Adventure of the Little Rooster at Wychwood Theatre, a family show from the team behind The Little Circus That Could.

events.description: From the team that brought you The Little Circus that Could and The Philip & Lucinda Dino-Show comes a new feather of a tale! Everything changes the day the Little Rooster finds a shiny silver coin. Hilarious consequences and supreme shenanigans abound! Dazzle and delight at this retelling of this beloved folk tale performed with music, dance, puppets, circus and cabbage!
events.address: 76 Wychwood Ave., Studio 176, Toronto, ON, M6G 4C7

title.en: 50 Years of Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery Exhibition - 50th Anniversary

ai.en: 50 Years of the Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery, a 50th-anniversary exhibition of artefacts, prints and paintings from City of Toronto collections.

events.description: Discover the history of art at the Etobicoke Civic Centre with artifacts, prints, images and paintings from City of Toronto’s Fine Art, Artifact and Archival collections. Celebrate the present by witnessing a commissioned piece by early career artist Lise Round. Envision the future with new designs of the updated Etobicoke Civic Centre Art Gallery.
events.address: 399 The West Mall, Etobicoke, ON, M9C 2Y2

ai.en: Storytime at the Park at Downsview Park, read-alouds in English and French, themed activities and nature play for children aged 3 to 9.

events.description: Perfect for families and children ages 3 to 9! Enjoy interactive read-alouds of beloved books in English and French, themed activities, nature exploration and a light snack. We can't wait to see you soon at Downsview Park!
events.address: 70 Canuck Ave, North York, ON, M3K 2C5

events.description: All started by a local student... We collect leftover wrapped candy for kids and families who need it, distributing through community food banks. Be part of this!!
events.address: Burnhamthorpe Mall, 666 Burnhamthorpe Rd, Etobicoke, ON M9C 2Z4

events.description: The 2-hour Apple Pie Class is beginner-friendly and teaches guests how to make flaky pie dough, roll it out, prepare apple filling, assemble the pie and decorate it with a lattice top or dough cutouts. Participants take home an unbaked 9-inch apple pie to bake at home or freeze for later, along with recipes emailed before class. All ingredients and equipment are provided. The class can be made vegan if the team is notified in advance. Aprons are available as an optional add-on.
events.address: 12 Sousa Mendes St, Toronto, ON, M6P 0A8

events.description: This 2-hour class is beginner-friendly and inspired by the JellyCat Amuseables collection. Guests learn how to fill and stack a heart-shaped cake, apply buttercream, create texture and sculpt fondant details to give their cake personality. Participants take home a fully decorated vanilla cake and receive vanilla cake, American buttercream and Swiss meringue buttercream recipes before class. All ingredients and equipment are provided, and aprons are available as an optional add-on.
events.address: 12 Sousa Mendes St, Toronto, ON, M6P 0A8

events.description: Celebrate the launch of Stories We Couldn't Keep to Ourselves, a picture book anthology written and illustrated by 16 youth authors from Scarborough’s Kingston-Galloway/Orton Park (KGO) neighbourhood. Developed during skill building workshops facilitated by professional authors and illustrators, this project features original stories inspired by the people and places within the KGO community. Enjoy author readings, a Q&A and family-friendly creative activities at this free event. Registration is required. All are welcome. A City of Toronto Cultural Hotspot Signature Project.
events.address: 4279 Lawrence Ave E, Scarborough, ON, M1E 2S8

ai.en: The 19th Pomegranate Film Festival at the Hamazkayin Theatre, celebrating Armenian stories and international cinema.

events.description: Returning for its 19th edition, celebrating Armenian stories and international cinema in Toronto. Discover compelling films, emerging filmmakers and stories that connect cultures, generations and communities. All films include English subtitles. Highlights include De Gaulle, a two part historical epic starring Simon Abkarian, with Q&As hosted by Oscar nominated Toronto filmmaker Atom Egoyan.
events.address: 50 Hallcrown Pl, North York, ON, M2J 1P7

title.en: The Sororum Presents: A Step Through Time

ai.en: A Step Through Time at the Bata Shoe Museum, a day of history, artistry and discovery in Yorkville.

events.description: Join us for a memorable day of history, artistry, discovery and meaningful connection in Toronto's charming Yorkville neighbourhood. Our journey begins at the iconic Bata Shoe Museum with a private guided tour exploring fascinating stories of Roman history and the artistry of beaded footwear across cultures. We'll then discover traditional leatherworking techniques and create our own keepsake. From there, we will gather at The Oxley, a charming Victorian townhouse, for a specially arranged prix fixe lunch and guided conversation, sharing perspectives and connecting with extraordinary women. More than an outing, it's an invitation to discover, connect and create lasting memories.
events.address: 327 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON M5S 1W7

title.en: Winter Crafts & Cozy Treats: Holiday Season at Scarborough Museum

events.description: Celebrate light, connection and community in a cozy historic setting each weekend. Enjoy hands-on family-friendly activities centered on food, culture and storytelling. Create festive winter crafts, gather around the fire and enjoy warm beverages and freshly baked treats prepared on the historic cast-iron stove. Learn stories behind seasonal foods and traditions, then share your own memories and experiences in a welcoming holiday food and storytelling circle.

title.en: Geoffrey James | Ancient and Modern: Selected Panoramas

events.description: The Stephen Bulger Gallery is pleased to present there second solo exhibition of work by Geoffrey James, one of Canada’s pre-eminent photographers. James’s panoramic photographs explore the relationship between people and the landscapes they create, shape, and transform. He became known for using a panoramic camera to photograph gardens, parks, cities, mines, and other human-made environments. His photographs are carefully composed and largely devoid of people. His images of formal European gardens reveal the ways in which humans organize and control nature, while later photographs of places such as mines and borders explore the more destructive consequences of human intervention.
events.address: 1356 Dundas St W, Toronto, ON, M6J 1Y2

title.en: Kensington Market ‘Taste the World’ Food Tour Fall 2026

ai.en: Taste the World, the original food tour of Kensington Market, visiting family-run shops and eateries beyond the tourist spots.

events.description: Explore Kensington Market with the tour that started it all! As the original food tour of one of Toronto’s quirkiest neighbourhoods, you will get to enjoy beyond the tourist traps to family-run shops, hidden counters, and must-try bites most visitors walk right past. Skip the lines and taste local favourites from around the world, from handmade Tibetan dumplings to flaky Jamaican patties. Thanks to our long-standing relationships with shop owners, you’ll get curated tastings from the market’s best spots. Come hungry, this tour counts as lunch! Along the way, you’ll hear the stories that shaped Kensington, from its roots as a Jewish market to today’s vibrant, multicultural neighbourhood. Led by locals who know the market inside and out, you’ll get insider access to the hidden corners and stories of Kensington that make the market special. Join us and discover the side of Kensington that most people miss!

title.en: Richard Avedon: Immortal: Portraits of Aging

ai.en: Immortal: Portraits of Aging at The Image Centre, Richard Avedon's photographs of ageing across nearly fifty years.

events.description: For nearly half a century, celebrated American photographer Richard Avedon confronted one of portraiture’s enduring taboos: aging. From his earliest years at Harper’s Bazaar, Avedon broke with the conventions of idealized celebrity portraiture, revealing the marks of time on his subjects’ faces with unsparing clarity. Bringing together nearly 100 portraits made between the early 1950s and 2004, the exhibition features artists, writers, musicians and cultural icons including Toni Morrison, Gabriel García Márquez, Duke Ellington, Ronald Reagan, the Duke and Duchess of Windsor, Patti Smith, Truman Capote and the Dalai Lama. Immortal also includes a restaging of Avedon’s seminal 1974 Museum of Modern Art exhibition Jacob Israel Avedon, which chronicled his father’s final years in nine extraordinary portraits. Taken as a whole, the photographs reveal a lesser-known dimension of Avedon’s practice and offer an unprecedented exploration of aging through his distinctive vision.

title.en: They Walked These Streets... and Answered the Call: Remembrance Installation at Fort York

ai.en: They Walked These Streets... and Answered the Call, a temporary remembrance installation at Fort York on Torontonians who served in war and on the home front.

events.description: Torontonians answered the call to war by enlisting in the armed forces, producing munitions and equipment and by helping on the home front. This temporary installation highlights stories of the people and places along Toronto’s waterfront that shaped the war effort from 1914 to 1918 and 1939 to 1945. Historical documents, photographs and artifacts honour the sacrifice of Torontonians, show how communities did their part and explain how Toronto, along the waterfront, was forever transformed by war. This installation is by They Walked These Streets, a Toronto-based community Remembrance Project.
events.address: 250 Fort York Blvd, Toronto, ON, M5V 3K9

ai.en: Molly Steels: I Am/Was/Always at The Image Centre, photography on how images hold moments against death.

events.description: The philosopher Diana Prokofyeva considers a photograph to be a phenomenon that exists as a way to avoid death by copying a moment and suspending it within time - a way to be between two worlds:, the living and the dead. She suggests that a photograph gives confidence of existence, a way to state, “Here I am and was, and always shall have been.”. View this evolving series that looks to photography as a method of conceptualizing grief and mortality. Using family archives from the past century and conceptual imagery, I locate myself within a chain of human experience. I look to the women who came before me, observing the proof of their existence with reverence and the knowledge that I will one day add to this catalogue. Through this series I aim to overshadow existential fear with curiosity. Ephemeral aspects of nature are woven into this work as both an unrelenting force and a source of comfort.

ai.en: Portent by Tanya Marcuse at The Image Centre, a multichannel video of ominous natural scenes such as swaying trees and volcanic vapour.

events.description: Tanya Marcuse’s multichannel video Portent presents ominous scenes of the natural world: trees swaying in the wind, vapour rising from volcanic fumaroles, icy branches illuminated by flickering light, and other small disturbances that hint at forces beyond our understanding. The quiet is deliberate; the frame remains fixed while the environment shifts restlessly within it, evoking a tension between stillness and motion, beauty and unease, the known and unknown. Marcuse describes her work as an exploration of the kinship between disaster and the sublime, and of the ways the world around us is continually threatened, transformed, and made strange. Portent forms part of her expansive series Book of Miracles (2020-26), inspired by the Augsburger Wunderzeichenbuch, a 16th-century illuminated manuscript depicting natural disasters, supernatural phenomena, celestial spectacles and unexplained oddities.

All tours are drop-in and free to attend. Please be aware that the trees in the park system are not yet mature, so there is little shade. We recommend dressing according to the weather. Tours are subject to cancellation in the event of adverse weather. Please see Lassonde Art Trail website for further details.

ai.en: Always In Fashion at the Textile Museum of Canada, curated by Amber-Dawn Bear Robe, on Indigenous design and its influence on fashion.

events.description: Curated by Amber-Dawn Bear Robe, enjoy an immersive exploration of Indigenous design languages and their transformative impact on the fashion landscape of the lands we call Canada and the United States. This exhibition emerges from the urgent need to recognize and celebrate Indigenous designers who are reshaping the industry by reclaiming cultural narratives, innovating with ancestral techniques, and challenging colonial frameworks within fashion. Through research on Indigenous fashion history, cultural sustainability, and decolonial design practices, the exhibition highlights how contemporary Indigenous couturiers blend ancestral knowledge with cutting-edge innovation to redefine fashion on their own terms.

events.description: Uncover hidden stories Toronto has long overlooked. Explore the history of over 70 historic sites, forgotten events, fascinating local narratives and unique objects. It surfaces the ignored, the hyperlocal and the quietly radical, reinforcing that history is not fixed, but layered and still unfolding. Museum of Toronto is bringing these stories to life through a physical exhibition alongside city-wide locations, inviting audiences to peel back the layers of Toronto. It’s both a tribute to the city’s past and a reminder that the places we pass every day hold unexpected and often untold stories.

title.en: Scarborough’s Delicious Secrets: Woks, Broths, and the Suburban Chinatown

ai.en: A food walk through Scarborough's Agincourt area, known as Asiancourt, and its East Asian restaurants at Lang Chai Authentic Vietnamese Cuisine.

events.description: Agincourt, also lovingly known as ‘Asiancourt’, is the beating heart of East Asian dining in Toronto, where unassuming strip plazas hide some of the most dynamic regional cooking in North America. On this tour, we will follow the flavours and stories that have shaped Agincourt across generations: from the fragrant lemongrass and herb-infused noodle broths of Vietnam, to deeply comforting, slow-simmered Korean pork-bone stews. We'll explore how northern Chinese charcoal-grilling traditions took hold alongside Cantonese staples as we sample cumin-dusted skewers and smoky street-style barbecue, before ending on a sweet note with a rich, multi-textured matcha parfait!

title.en: Remembering GECO Girls of Scarborough at Scarborough Museum

events.description: Join author and local historian Barbara Dickson for a presentation on Bomb Girls: Trading Aprons for Ammo and explore the stories of Scarborough's own GECO Girls. View a pop-up panel highlighting the women who worked at the GECO munitions factory, Canada's largest fuse-filling munitions factory during the Second World War, and learn about their contributions and sacrifices to the war effort. Through storytelling and historical research, discover the experiences of workers aged 17 to 70 from diverse cultural backgrounds and gain insight into an important chapter of Scarborough's history. After the presentation, there's a book signing with a limited number of copies available for purchase.

title.en: Sala-Manca Group: Like a Bird’s Nest

ai.en: Like a Bird's Nest, a retrospective of the Sala-Manca Group at PIX FILM Gallery, with installation, video and photography shown together for the first time.

events.description: Enjoy a landmark retrospective from the international artist collective, the Sala-Manca Group. Installation, video and photography are exhibited together for the first time, all connected to the ritual object of the sukkah, a temporary hut traditionally erected during the Jewish festival of Sukkot. Over the last twenty years, Sala-Manca has explored the symbolism and function of the sukkah and related themes of shelter, impermanence, displacement, and liberation. In their hands, the sukkah is interchangeably a ritual structure, an ethnographic object, a work of art, an ephemeral monument, a site of protest, and a performative arena. This exhibition traverses unlikely geographies, travelling through time and place, from a small town in Germany where no Jews remain to a Jahalin Bedouin community in Khan al-Ahmar; from the contested streets of Jerusalem to the fraught landscapes of Ontario.

ai.en: K-Pop Dreamworld at the Lyric Theatre, a K-Pop tribute show with music and visual spectacle.

events.description: K-Pop Dreamworld: The Ultimate K-Pop Tribute Experience Step into a vibrant universe where music and imagination collide in K-Pop Dreamworld, a high-energy tribute show celebrating the global K-Pop phenomenon. This visually stunning production features three powerhouse West End vocalists supported by world-class dancers performing a soundtrack inspired by the hit movie KPop Demon Hunters, and the record-breaking hits of BTS, BLACKPINK, Jennie, and Rosé. While the show delivers the explosive choreography and cinematic visuals fans crave, it also carries a moving message about the magic of believing in yourself. From viral anthems to electrifying stage moments, this immersive tribute experience captures the undeniable energy of the genre. Join us for an unforgettable night that invites every audience member to dream big, follow their dreams and believe in themselves - all whilst celebrating the music that conquered the world.

ai.en: Goodnight Desdemona (Good Morning Juliet) at the Bluma Appel Theatre, a comedy that reworks Shakespeare's heroines, marking the play's 40th anniversary.

events.description: A joyful comedy that flips the script on Shakespeare's most infamous heroines. To celebrate the 40th anniversary of her landmark play, acclaimed novelist and playwright Ann-Marie MacDonald steps into the spotlight as Constance Ledbelly, the overlooked academic who tumbles headlong into Shakespeare’s worlds and discovers that the heroines (and even Constance herself) may be capable of far more than anyone imagined. At once wildly funny and moving, this Canadian classic unleashes Desdemona and Juliet as fierce forces of their own destiny and reminds us that sometimes the bravest act is claiming your own story.

Players will enter a twisted study of horror, where their knowledge of classic slasher films is just as important as their ability to solve puzzles, crack codes and escape within an hour. Think you can tell Saw from Scream? Know your Halloween from your Friday the 13th? You’ll need that knowledge, and a little nerve, to make it out.

ai.en: A Christmas Carol at the Fleck at Harbourfront Centre Theatre, a fresh adaptation of Dickens's story by Tim Carroll.

events.description: Dickens’s timeless holiday story of transformation, kindness and human connection. This fresh adaptation by Tim Carroll brings Charles Dickens’s world to life through inventive puppetry, towering ghosts that fill the stage, traditional carols and audience participation with spirited sing-alongs. Interactive performers mingle throughout the theatre, while beautifully detailed period costumes and sets create an atmospheric Victorian Christmas. More than 175 years after Dickens first published A Christmas Carol, audiences still recognize themselves in Ebenezer Scrooge: someone who discovers that it’s never too late in life to choose kindness and human connection. For centuries, this iconic story has endured because its themes are still relevant today: What really matters to us? And can people truly change?

ai.en: Immersion Festival at the Betty Oliphant Theatre, a celebration of Canadian performing arts with showcases and networking.

events.description: Join us for a celebration of Canadian cultural life for audiences and a sought-after performance and networking opportunity for renowned and aspiring artists, with three distinct stage performances, twelve workshops, a dance education roundtable, and community gatherings. Performances and workshops are open to all! Enjoy The Vanguard Presentation includes commissioned works by Katlyn Addison and Tanya Charles, Travis Knights and Divine Brown, and Nubian Néné. The National Presentation features Ebnflōh Dance Company, Lua Shayenne Dance Company, and N.A.P.P.Y. Dance, while the Next Gen showcase highlights emerging Black youth artists. Our workshops for youth, beginners, and professionals are led by Kwasi Obeng-Adjei, Reequal Smith, Natasha Powell, and Isaac Gasangwa, exploring diverse Black and diasporic movement practices. Three gathering events bring together presenters, artists, and academics to connect, exchange ideas, and celebrate Black dance across Canada.

ai.en: Rogers v. Rogers at the Berkeley Street Theatre, a play based on the book about the battle for control of Canada's Rogers telecom empire.

events.description: The hit show returns to a new venue, same buzz! Based on Rogers v. Rogers: The Battle for Control of Canada’s Telecom Empire by Alexandra Posadzki. Telecom tycoon Ted Rogers built an empire turning Canada’s airwaves into cash. Now his son Edward, long dismissed by his father, is fighting for control of the family business. Meanwhile, shrewd public servant Matthew Boswell is determined to derail Rogers’ billion-dollar takeover of Shaw Communications. From award-winning playwright Michael Healey (The Master Plan, The Drawer Boy) and starring Tom Rooney (Fifteen Dogs, Uncle Vanya) comes a story of outsized ambition, personal grudges, and corporate power. Inspired by one of the most dramatic boardroom showdowns in Canadian history, this riveting new drama examines the price of pushing back, the unraveling bonds of kin, and the legacy that money can and cannot buy.

ai.en: Macbeth at Crow's Theatre, a solo performance of Shakespeare's tragedy about Macbeth's climb to power.

events.description: One prophecy. One performer. Total collapse. Shakespeare’s most haunting tragedy traces Macbeth’s ruthless climb to power in this solo performance, set against the cutthroat world of the modern tech industry. One prophecy sets the scene for Macbeth’s terrifying unraveling, where every thought, every fear, every choice pushes him beyond the point of no return. In this electrifying reimagining, the collision of unstoppable technology and human free will forces us to confront the fragility - and ferocity - of the human spirit. Discover what happens when the scale of a Shakespearean tragedy is transformed into a gripping ninety-minute performance. Evan Buliung, one of Canada's leading stage actors and veteran of twelve seasons at the Stratford Festival, returns to Crow's after his acclaimed performance as Pierre in Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812.

ai.en: The Cut, a world premiere at the Miriam Green Theatre, co-produced with Winnipeg Jewish Theatre and written by Jordi Mand.

events.description: World Premiere The Cut A coproduction with Winnipeg Jewish Theatre Written By Jordi Mand Directed by Philip Akin In the nursery of their soon-to-be-born child, Sarah and Drew are unpacking boxes and preparing for a new beginning. But when the question of circumcision arises, the ordinary quickly turns urgent. Raised in deeply different religious traditions, this couple finds themselves locked in a raw and revealing debate about their baby's future - and their own. What starts as a single decision opens into buried wounds, unspoken regrets, and the fault lines of love and belief. The Cut is an intimate, gripping two-hander about faith, identity, and partnership at a breaking point - asking what it truly takes to build a future when fundamental values collide. 2025 Carol Bolt Award Recipient for In Seven Days "Mand's dialogue is fast-paced, witty... a touching sense of shared experience between the story and its audience." - Eden Eidt
events.venue: Meridian Arts Centre: Miriam Green Theatre

ai.en: Aga Khan Master Musicians at Koerner Hall, music rooted in the Middle East, Mediterranean, South and Central Asia and China.

events.description: Creating music inspired by their own deep roots in the cultures of the Middle East and Mediterranean Basin, South Asia, Central Asia, and China. Brought together by the Aga Khan Music Programme to explore how musical innovation can contribute to the revitalization of cultural heritage, the Master Musicians are venerated performers and composer-arrangers who appear on the world’s most prestigious stages while also serving as preeminent teachers, mentors, and curators. Each of these exceptional artists has achieved mastery within a rigorous musical tradition defined by canonical styles, repertoires, pedagogy, and performance techniques. Retracing Tatreez highlights what these belongings can tell us about the relationship between Palestinians and their homelands in the twentieth century and beyond. In this exhibition, curator Nina Rafique showcases these pieces with restored historical context and invites visitors to re-engage with their ways of storytelling. CALIGARI is a 1920 German silent horror film, directed by Robert Wiene and written by Hans Janowitz and Carl Mayer. Considered the quintessential work of German Expressionist cinema, it tells the story of an insane hypnotist (Werner Krauss) who uses a somnambulist (Conrad Veidt) to commit murders. The film features a dark and twisted visual style, with sharp-pointed forms, oblique and curving lines, structures and landscapes that lean and twist in unusual angles, and shadows and streaks of light painted directly onto the sets. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IAtpxqajFak NASH THE SLASH composed the musical scores for these and several other classic silent films and would perform them live at each screening. title.en: Benedict Sheehan’s ‘Ukrainian War Requiem’: The National Tour

ai.en: Benedict Sheehan's Ukrainian War Requiem, a national tour at St. Paul's Basilica by the Axios Men's Ensemble, a Juno-winning group.

events.description: The Axios Men’s Ensemble, in celebration of their historic Juno award, for Classical Album of the Year (Large Ensemble) for the recording of Benedict Sheehan’s Ukrainian War Requiem, have announced a national tour this November. Composed by two-time Grammy-Nominated Benedict Sheehan, this monumental choral work spans 12 impactful movements that seamlessly blend modern musical styles with ancient chants and traditional Ukrainian motifs. The choral tribute serves as a powerful musical reverence for those affected by the war, offering solace and strength to the living and the grieving, and ultimately providing a solemn space for remembrance and prayer through a skillful and heartfelt tribute to Ukraine and her people. Conducted by Maestro Michael Zaugg, the choir features over 50 performers from Axios Men’s Ensemble, Pro Coro Canada and international soloists. More than music, Ukrainian War Requiem is a journey through grief that reminds us of the enduring grace of the human spirit.

events.description: AZNAVOUR AND THE LEGENDS NOVEMBER 15 - TORONTO A breathtaking tribute celebrating the timeless music of Charles Aznavour and the greatest voices of French chanson. After the success of his 2024 Canadian tour and performances in Paris, Venice, Belgrade, Yerevan, Dubai, Brussels, Alexandria and beyond, internationally acclaimed singer and pianist Ghassan Yammine returns to North America. With his warm, expressive voice remarkably reminiscent of Aznavour, Yammine brings these legendary songs to life alongside live musicians. Experience classics by Charles Aznavour, Édith Piaf, Jacques Brel, Yves Montand, Gilbert Bécaud and more - from "La Bohème" and "Hier Encore" to "La Vie en Rose," "Ne Me Quitte Pas" and "Les Feuilles Mortes." events.description: "Letter midwife" Frish Brandt joins geriatrician Dr. Samir Sinha for a conversation presented in conjunction with Richard Avedon Immortal. Brandt was Richard Avedon’s longtime art dealer at San Francisco’s Fraenkel Gallery before becoming a “letter midwife.” She joins Dr. Samir Sinha, one of Canada’s foremost geriatricians and a leading expert on societal aging for a conversation presented in conjunction with the exhibition Richard Avedon Immortal. Brandt will share stories from her years working with Avedon, as well as insights from her current practice helping people write important letters to the people they care about most. events.description: Discover a lesser-known chapter of Canadian history celebrating democracy and solidarity at a special documentary screening. In 1991, approximately 80 young Canadians and Americans of Ukrainian descent, including many participants from Toronto, travelled to Ukraine to support its independence movement ahead of the December 1 referendum. Through rare archival footage and firsthand accounts, the documentary explores Canadian civic engagement, international solidarity and the power of individuals to advance democracy. On December 2, 1991, Canada became the first Western country to recognize Ukraine's independence. Thirty-five years later, the film highlights Toronto's connections to global history as Ukraine continues to defend its sovereignty. Join us on November 18 for a story of courage and civic responsibility, followed by a discussion and Q&A with the filmmakers.

events.description: Samuel Beckett’s Endgame is the tragicomic tale of a man living with his parents and his servant in a world beyond time and place. With nowhere to go and not much to do, they spend their days telling stories and contemplating the absurdity of life. Directed by Druid’s Tony Award-winning Artistic Director Garry Hynes, the first woman to win the Tony for Best Director (Martin McDonagh’s The Beauty Queen of Leenane), Endgame stars Druid Ensemble members Aaron Monaghan, Rory Nolan and Tony Award-winner Marie Mullen, with Bosco Hogan. Endgame follows Druid’s award-winning 2016 production of Beckett’s Waiting for Godot, which toured the world for three years, wowing audiences and critics alike. "It’s awfully good to be in their company… the fine, funny artists of Garry Hynes’s venerable Druid troupe" – The New York Times Critic's Pick.

ai.en: Dog Days, a Canadian opera premiere at the Nancy and Ed Jackman Performance Centre, mixing classical voice with dark ambient sound and electric guitar.

events.description: A contemporary opera that combines classical vocals with dark ambient noise and amplified electric guitars. Set during a fictional wartime blackout, the story follows a rural working-class family attempting to survive amidst military collapse and severe food shortages. The psychological drama explores human resilience, desperation, and moral breakdown when social structures disintegrate. Critically acclaimed by The New York Times, this breakthrough work from the writing team of composer David T. Little (Soldier Songs, JFK) and Canadian librettist Royce Vavrek (Angel’s Bone, Listen, Quiet) put them on the map. They have since gone on, both together and in collaboration with others, to revolutionize opera in North America.

Young musicians from our special guests, the Etobicoke Suzuki School bring a fresh energy to the stage, performing their own favourites and joining our strings for Jorge Vargas’ La Bruja. The Naghash Ensemble combines the earthy spirituality of Armenian folk songs, new classical music, and contemporary post-minimalism with the energy of rock and jazz. Three brilliant female vocalists and some of Armenia’s finest instrumentalists on duduk, oud, dhol, and piano play captivating new music based on sacred texts by the medieval Armenian mystic poet and priest Mkrtich Naghash.

Celebrating South Asian Canadian diversity of yesterday, today and tomorrow.

title.en: The Stories We Keep: A Writing and Storytelling Workshop

events.description: Bring an object that matters to you and spend an afternoon exploring the memories, people, places, and moments held within the objects we keep through writing, reflection, and conversation. Led by a former archaeologist, you'll use guided prompts and archaeology-inspired approaches to uncover the stories and meaning behind one meaningful object from home. Enjoy a relaxed, small-group experience with writing exercises, conversation, and time for personal reflection. A workbook and all writing materials will be provided. No previous writing experience is needed, and sharing your story is entirely optional. Your object can be anything, from an old photograph or piece of jewellery to a childhood toy, handwritten note, or everyday item with a special memory attached. The object doesn't need to be valuable or old. What matters is the story it carries for you.

ai.en: The Toronto Artists Symphony Orchestra's Symphony Concert 2026 at the George Weston Recital Hall, with orchestral and piano works.

events.description: The Toronto Artists Symphony Orchestra presents an extraordinary evening of orchestral and piano masterpieces featuring internationally acclaimed pianist Sofia Gulyak, one of the most distinguished pianists of her generation and winner of numerous international awards. This captivating program brings together some of the most beloved works from the classical repertoire, highlighting the music of Tchaikovsky and Rachmaninoff. The evening also features the Suite from The Red Detachment of Women, one of the most celebrated and recognizable works in Chinese musical culture. Based on the landmark ballet of the same name, the suite tells a powerful story of courage, determination, and social change. Its memorable themes, vibrant orchestral colors, and dramatic energy have made it a beloved favorite throughout China and among audiences around the world. The work remains an important symbol of Chinese artistic heritage and continues to be performed by orchestras internationally.

title.en: Sisters in Songs: Daughters of Donbas - Hildá Länsman & Tuomas Norvio - GETCHNAH

events.description: Join us for an evening of music and sisterhood. The musicians will take you on a journey inspired by cultures and corners of the world, rooted in different traditions and singing stories often overlooked. Daughters of Donbas is an all-female and non-binary ensemble featuring Ukrainian singer Marichka an activist, war journalist, volunteer combat medic and winner of the Amnesty International Award. Hildá Länsman and Tuomas Norvio invite you to join their ongoing exploration between the ancient Sámi vocal tradition of luohti and modern electronic soundscapes. GETCHNAH is an artist who is celebrated for her electrifying live performances and graced major national stages with her undeniable talent, such as the Canadian National Exhibition. events.description: The Student Galleries mark OCAD University’s 150th anniversary with a pointed declaration of purpose by positioning the institution not merely as a site of technical training or aesthetic refinement, but rather as a long-standing incubator of creative disruption. The exhibition gathers notable alumni and long-time faculty whose practices embody this refusal. These artists do not form a school or style, but rather what binds them is a shared willingness to step across boundaries, to trouble conventions and to keep culture unsettled in the interest of possibility. The exhibition is both celebration and summons: a recognition of what has been achieved and an invitation to keep the boundaries moving.

events.description: Listen to the story of Robert Baldwin, one of the strangest and most pivotal figures in Canadian history. Not everyone who demanded change believed in violence. One of the leading champions of Canadian democracy refused to take up arms and join the rebels. Baldwin's summer home was located where the museum is today. Investigate the role Baldwin played in trying to find a peaceful solution to the rebellion crisis, how he eventually accomplished what Mackenzie never did, and the bizarre twist to his tragic love story. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

ai.en: Song for a Winter's Day at the Jane Mallett Theatre, a midwinter concert based on Susan Cooper's The Shortest Day.

events.description: Susan Cooper's The Shortest Day looks across centuries of midwinter tradition: fires burning through the night, homes hung with evergreen, and people singing and dancing against the dark. At the heart of CCOC's Winter Concert is a staged telling of Cooper's poem, woven throughout the performance. Choral music brings its imagery to life: from snowfall and candlelight to celebration and the promise of returning light. CCOC's young artists perform works by Marie-Claire Saindon, Katerina Gimon, Benjamin Britten, Amy Beach, John Beckwith and more, accompanied by live musicians. The concert also features the world premiere of Soir d'hiver by CCOC pianist Stéphane Mayer. Both performances conclude with a cherished company tradition: Gordon Lightfoot's Song for a Winter's Night, arranged by Chris and Charissa Bagan. Join us for a winter gathering alive with story, song and the joyful sound of young voices.

title.en: Curator’s Talk: Time, Labour and the Value of Beads

ai.en: A curator's talk at the Bata Shoe Museum on the history and value of beads, in connection with the Brilliant exhibition.

events.description: Beads may be small and intricate, but their histories reveal powerful stories of identity, value, and status. In celebration of Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear Around the World, join Director and Senior Curator Elizabeth Semmelhack for an informative and illuminating exploration of beadwork traditions from around the world and their role as markers of wealth, prestige, and cultural meaning. From royal adornment and ceremonial regalia to trade and personal expression, this lecture traces how beads have signaled belonging across time and place. At its core is the labour behind the work: the skilled craftsmanship, generational knowledge, and cultural practices embedded in every stitch. By centering time and labour, the talk challenges conventional ideas of value and asks what makes something “luxurious,” and who defines luxury.

ai.en: TD Encounters: Orison at Hugh's Room, a musical collaboration by Daniel Áñez and James O'Callaghan that blends science fiction imagery with prayer.

events.description: Orison (prayer) is a musical collaboration from musician Daniel Áñez and composer James O’Callaghan, connecting science fiction imagery with spirituality and the idea of ‘alien-ness’ in all of its senses: social, cultural, psychological, extra-terrestrial. The work centres the unique early electronic instrument, the ondes Martenot, as a jumping-off point to interact with synthesized soundscapes, field recordings, techno, poetic text, and documentary-like spoken confessionals. Featuring Ánez on the incredibly evocative ondes Martenot, with O’Callaghan on electronics, this Encounters event presents the current musical stage in the development of a new music theatre work. Audiences will experience fragments, improvisatory excerpts, and other material from this long-term work in progress, offering a rare opportunity to engage with the creative process as the piece continues to evolve. Please join us for this unique musical experience.

Symposium: A Black History of Photography

events.description: Join us for a day of talks by international scholars and artists examining photography through the lens of Black history and experience. From the invention of photography, Black populations across the globe have been at the forefront of the technology’s innovation and social use. For many Black people living in the 19th and 20th centuries, photography served as a source of income, a platform for community building and political mobilization and as a component of everyday interaction. Black use and innovation of the medium have long unfolded beyond the gaze and support of Western fine arts museums and universities. The history of photography is littered with universalisms that fail to capture the complex and diverse networks of circulation and innovation adopted by Black people.

title.en: A Black History of Photography: A Short Introduction with Drew Thompson

events.description: In this keynote lecture, Dr. Drew Thompson introduces the questions and themes that guide the Black History of Photography symposium. What does a black history of photography actually look like? This talk takes up such a proposition. He will consider Blackness in the history of photography through the lens of form and color as well as from the perspective of Black populations. Dr. Thompson argues through a range of historical and cultural examples from the late 19th century to the present moment that Blackness and Black life bring something urgent and essential to the history of photography.

events.description: Raised in northern Indiana, Josie Edwards formed her first band in high school before moving to Nashville to study at Belmont University, where she earned a degree in songwriting. She carried that momentum through “The Poet and Her Vice (Happy Ending),” “Dog Prophecies” and “Gravedigger,” into her 2026 EP Greetings From Bleak St. Its standout track, “Chemical Light,” has sparked another wave of attention online and pushed her audience higher still. Drawing on artists like Tom Odell, Twenty One Pilots, Noah Kahan, The Lumineers and Bob Dylan, Josie pairs dark humor with folk-pop melodies that stick. It’s an identity entirely her own — and one of the most distinct arriving in the genre right now.

events.description: NOVA: After The Music is a powerful new dance production inspired by the story of a survivor of the Nova Music Festival massacre on October 7, 2023. Through contemporary dance, music, and immersive theatrical storytelling, the production traces a journey from the freedom and joy of the festival through terror, survival, grief, and ultimately resilience. Grounded in a real survivor's experience, NOVA: After The Music is both a deeply personal story and a collective act of remembrance. The production honours the lives that were lost, gives space to the stories of those who survived, and explores what it means to carry memory forward after unimaginable loss. It is a moving tribute to life, humanity, and the enduring strength to keep dancing after the music stops.
events.venue: Meridian Arts Centre: Miriam Green Theatre

ai.en: Constantinople: Oum Kalthoum and the Quatrains of Khayyam at the George Weston Recital Hall, linking Omar Khayyam's poetry with Oum Kalthoum's music.

events.description: Constantinople: Oum Kalthoum & the Quatrains of Khayyam The timeless poetry of Omar Khayyam meets the unforgettable musical world of Oum Kalthoum in this extraordinary performance by Constantinople with Ghalia Benali. Reimagined through Persian and Arabic musical traditions, early music, contemporary composition, and live improvisation, the performance brings poetry, voice, and music into conversation across centuries. Songs inspired by Khayyam's quatrains, composed by Riad El Sonbati and made famous through Oum Kalthoum's interpretations, become the starting point for a new artistic journey. Led by Iranian-Canadian composer and setar virtuoso Kiya Tabassian, Constantinople is joined by Tunisian-Belgian vocalist Ghalia Benali, whose deep connection to Oum Kalthoum's repertoire brings insight, presence, and a distinctive contemporary voice. This concert is part of Ishq Festival 2026, produced by Small World Music.

title.en: Music Toronto - Gryphon Trio with James Campbell

ai.en: Music Toronto presents the Gryphon Trio with James Campbell at the Jane Mallett Theatre, playing Messiaen's Quartet for the End of Time.

events.description: In its early years as a Music Toronto ensemble-in-residence, the Gryphon Trio first performed Olivier Messiaen’s visionary "Quartet for the End of Time" with revered Canadian clarinetist James Campbell. Composed in a prisoner-of-war camp during the Second World War, the work stands as one of the 20th century’s most profound musical testaments of faith, transcendence and human resilience. Twenty-five years and countless performances later, the Gryphon Trio and Campbell return to this monumental masterpiece that has become a defining thread in their artistic story. The program opens with the stormy passion of Johannes Brahms’ dramatic Piano Trio in C minor and also features the world premiere of a new work for piano trio by Graham Campbell.

events.description: A journey into the realm of memory. Lepage plunges into the depths of memory and questions the relevance of certain recollections. Why do we remember the phone number from our youth, yet forget our current one? How does a childhood song withstand the test of time, while the name of a loved one escapes us? Why does meaningless information stay with us, while other, more useful information falls away? The show considers various commemorative markers and the historical heritage around us that we no longer notice. The play also focuses on oblivion, the unconscious and memory that fades over time, whose limits are now compensated for by digital storage, mountains of data and virtual memory. Somewhere between theatre performance and conference, Lepage reveals the suffering of an actor who must remember not only his text, but also his past, as well as the historical and social realities that have shaped his identity.
events.address: 189 Yonge St, Toronto, ON M5B 1M4, Canada

title.en: ‘Twas the Night Before...by Cirque du Soleil

This exhilarating show transforms the classic tale into an acrobatic winter wonderland filled with laughter, heart and breathtaking acrobatic feats. When the magic of the poem comes to life, a young girl and her father are unexpectedly separated by a snowstorm that sends them on a fantastical journey through whimsical places and encounters with memorable characters who help them to reignite the holiday spirit and true meaning of Christmas. A cheerful sing-along, dance-along and imagine-along extravaganza full of surprises from reindeer hoop divers to breakdancing elves and an awe-inspiring roller skating duo, blending festive fun and gravity defying spectacle into a tradition that families will cherish.

title.en: Rebellion Talks: The Rebels' Island Stronghold

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Todmorden Mills on the Rebels' island stronghold and the aftermath of the Rebellion of 1837.

events.description: Learn about the violent aftermath of the Rebellion of 1837. The revolutionaries didn't give up easily. Even after Mackenzie's army was crushed at the Battle of Montgomery's Tavern, the rebels kept fighting. They rallied new supporters as they seized control of an island in the Niagara River, declared it to be the independent Republic of Canada, and launched what became known as the Patriot War. It's a story of bloody battles, revolutionary spies, pirate admirals, and two competing visions for the future of the continent. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Journey through a winter landscape of sound, where voices capture the beauty, stillness and wonder of the season. Celebrating both the winter season and the human journey through time and space, this programme explores the cycles of life, change and renewal. Through evocative melodies and rich harmonies, the music reflects a world in constant evolution, where endings and beginnings come together in a continuous, beautiful cycle. Complicity rarely announces itself. From Tony- and Oscar-winning writer Christopher Hampton and based on the real-life testimony of Brunhilde Pomsel, secretary to Joseph Goebbels in 1940s Germany, A German Life traces one woman’s extraordinary life inside a regime built on propaganda and terror. At the age of 103, Pomsel looks back and recounts her work, her choices and her daily survival. Hampton’s adaptation examines the incremental slide – the quiet rationalizations and small concessions through which ordinary people become entangled in extraordinary evil. A German Life is a meditation on memory, guilt and the fragile line between complicity and innocence. The play, directed by Stewart Arnott, stars Canadian theatre legend Fiona Reid, whose work has been seen across the country at Stratford, Shaw and beyond, including on film, in My Big Fat Greek Wedding and The Time Traveler’s Wife, and on Broadway, in Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.

Smart, topical, and wickedly witty, this is a workplace comedy about generational change and the risky business of revisiting the past.

title.en: Rebellion Talks: Riots & the Rebel Mayor

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Mackenzie House on the riots that shook Toronto before and after the Rebellion of 1837.

events.description: Learn about the riots that shook Toronto to its core in the years before and after the Rebellion of 1837 in the rebel mayor’s former home, which is now Mackenzie House Museum. Political violence was a common occurrence in Toronto; rival factions battled in our streets. Hear the history behind the riots that helped convince Mackenzie that an armed revolution was his only option and explore the riots that continued to rage long after his rebellion was over. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Please join us for an unforgettable evening with Bertrand Chamayou, one of today’s most strikingly brilliant pianists, as he performs a program celebrating the Romantic and French repertoires! Chamayou has been recognised for his revelatory performances, at once powerfully virtuosic, imaginative and breathtakingly beautiful. A leading interpreter of French music, his vast repertoire includes major bodies of work such as the complete piano works of Ravel, Liszt’s Etudes and Années de Pèlerinage, and Messiaen's Vingt regards sur l'Enfant Jésus. He performs regularly with fellow musicians including cellist Sol Gabetta and is creating a Messiaen project with soprano-conductor Barbara Hannigan, with whom he performed in Koerner Hall in 2024. events.description: We welcome you to join us for this special performance. title.en: Marian Hill ACT TWO: THE TOUR

ai.en: Marian Hill's ACT TWO tour at The Great Hall in Toronto. The American electronic pop duo of vocalist Samantha Gongol and producer Jeremy Lloyd blends moody electronics and jazz-influenced saxophone.

events.description: Marian Hill is an American electronic pop duo made up of vocalist Samantha Gongol and producer Jeremy Lloyd. Their sound blends moody electronics, jazz-influenced saxophone, and Gongol's distinctive vocals into a style that's sleek, intimate, and hard to categorize --- somewhere between R&B, pop, and avant-garde electronic music. They arrived on the scene in 2013 when their single , "rdquo" -> One Time" went viral on Vine. Before long, their song Got It was in one of the first Today's Top Hits playlists as well as a Taco Bell commercial, leading them to sign with Republic Records. They embarked on their first national tour and a radio campaign followed, peaking with One Time at #38 on US Alt Radio. Their big breakthrough came a few years later when their single "Down" was featured in Apple's AirPods ad, pairing Gongol's smoky vocals and a sparse piano line with a stuttering electronic beat --- making it one of the most Shazamed songs in the country. The track reached No. 21 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was recently certified double platinum. Their music has been in major commercials for All State, Calvin Klein, Hyundai and Fox Sports and seen on TV in HBO's Industry, Lucifer, Santa Clarita Diet, So You Think You Can Dance and Dancing with the Stars. They've performed at Coachella, Lollapalooza, Bonaroo, Electric Forest, Firefly, Governor's Ball, and more and played to sold out crowds abroad in China, Korea, Japan and all over Europe. events.description: Dancing at the edge of history. Few musicals feel as essential to revisit or as urgent to re-examine as Cabaret. Set in Berlin as the shadows of extremism lengthen, Cabaret invites us into a world of music, seduction and dangerous denial. title.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band presents Brass Tango

ai.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band presents Brass Tango at Jane Mallett Theatre in Toronto, with the Payadora Tango Ensemble and a 10-piece brass ensemble celebrating Latin American music.

events.description: An exhilarating celebration of the music, rhythms, and traditions of Latin America. Featuring the acclaimed Payadora Tango Ensemble alongside a specially assembled 10-piece Hannaford brass ensemble, this concert brings together the raw passion of tango with the power, brilliance, and versatility of brass. The collaboration between Payadora Tango Ensemble and the Hannaford brass ensemble creates an exciting musical dialogue between two powerful instrumental worlds. The intimacy, flexibility, and rhythmic subtlety of the tango ensemble meet the expansive sound and thrilling sonority of brass, creating fresh perspectives on music that is built on movement, passion, and groove. With its combination of virtuosity, infectious rhythms, dramatic melodies, and vibrant cultural traditions, Brass Tango promises an unforgettable concert experience.

title.en: Warner Bros. Discovery presents Bugs Bunny at the Symphony

ai.en: Bugs Bunny at the Symphony at Meridian Hall in Toronto, with 16 classic Looney Tunes projected on screen. Ages 5 and up. The concert marks Bugs Bunny's 85th birthday and its 35th anniversary.

events.description: Age Suitability 5+. This beloved concert has played to millions all over the world with over 300 major symphony orchestras, and now returns to Toronto just in time to celebrate Bugs Bunny's 85th Birthday, and the concert's 35th Anniversary. Sixteen classic Looney Tunes will be projected on the big screen, as the FILMharmonique Orchestra conducted by George Daugherty, performs the original, iconic scores LIVE as inspired by Wagner, Rossini, Donizetti, Johann Strauss, Liszt, Smetana, Mendelssohn, Ponchielli, von Suppé, and others. Don't miss Baton Bunny, The Rabbit of Seville, What's Opera, Doc?, Corny Concerto, Long-Haired Hare, and many other brilliant and beloved animated masterpieces. Plus the WORLD PREMIERE of the brand new Skyscraper Scrap starring Tweety and Sylvester, a just-completed animated short saluting Bugs' 85 years on the silver screen, and a suite of three new Wile E. Coyote/Road Runner 3D shorts. It's the ultimate version of this cherished concert!

events.description: Virtuoso Spanish violinist Leticia Moreno leads an ensemble with piano, bandoneon, and bass in a program of works that explore the dialogue between Baroque tradition and the vibrant musical languages of the Americas. Recognised as a truly exciting and versatile violinist, Moreno has collaborated alongside Sol Gabetta, Bertrand Chamayou, and Kirill Gerstein and was the youngest member of the prestigious Alexander von Humboldt Stiftung. She has won international violin competitions such as the Henryk Szeryng International violin competition, Concertino Praga, Pablo Sarasate International Violin Competition, as well as being awarded with the ECHO Rising Star. events.description: Founded at the Royal Conversatory of Music to honour the sesquicentennial, Canada’s global orchestra celebrates its 10th anniversary. KUNÉ, Canada’s Global Orchestra, was intended as a one-night-only showcase to celebrate Canada’s cultural diversity and pluralism. Now, 10 years and two albums later, the ensemble seeks to communicate in ways that words, politicians, and spiritual leaders cannot, and help to find a common language through music. The musicians hail from all corners of the globe (Peru, Burkina Faso, Cuba, Ukraine, and beyond) and play instruments as diverse as they are, from the tar of Iran to the bouzouki of Greece to the clarinet of Türkiye. After the concert, enjoy a beverage and more music at the Postlude Performance featuring a local emerging artist.

Featuring four powerhouse vocalists and spectacular dancers, this immersive production brings Michael Jackson's repertoire to life through unforgettable performances, iconic choreography, and breathtaking energy. Step into a universe inspired by Smooth Criminal, one of Michael Jackson's most iconic music videos. In a mysterious speakeasy reminiscent of the Roaring Twenties, the music comes alive as the performers immerse you in the environment. From his greatest dance anthems to his most powerful ballads, experience the songs that defined generations. The excitement builds through the evening, culminating in a finale that transforms the theatre into an unforgettable celebration of the music and legacy of the King of Pop. It's not a musical. It's not a concert. It's an event. A celebration. An experience.

title.en: A Beethoven Celebration with John O’Conor

ai.en: A Beethoven Celebration with John O'Conor at Mazzoleni Concert Hall, marking the Irish pianist's 80th birthday with Glenn Gould School students.

events.description: Irish pianist John O’Conor celebrates his 80th birthday with Beethoven, joined by Glenn Gould School students and a special duet piano performance with James Anagnoson, Dean Emeritus of the GGS and Piano Department Chair. "A pianist of unbounding sensitivity" (Gramophone), O'Conor is renowned globally for his masterly playing over the last 50 years. A Steinway Artist, he is Chair of the Piano Division at Shenandoah University in Virginia, Professor of Piano at The Glenn Gould School, Distinguished Visiting Artist at the TU Dublin Conservatoire of Music and Visiting Professor at Showa University in Japan. Anagnoson is one of Canada's best-known pianists and pedagogues. He has been on the piano faculty of the Glenn Gould School since its formation in 1987 and has also taught at the University of Toronto and the University of Western Ontario. Presented in honour of Canada-Ireland 180.

events.description: Featuring one of the most evocative instruments in the orchestra and a world premiere written for the evening's soloist. Harpist Teresa Suen-Campbell, whose recent album with Sinfonia Toronto was praised as "a splendid presentation" by Textura and celebrated for its "warmth, clarity and emotional depth" by Harp Column, takes centre stage for the world premiere of Alice Ping Yee Ho's Beneath the Sea of Time, a harp concerto commissioned by Sinfonia Toronto that uses the sea as a metaphor for memory, loss, and renewal. Pianist Theadora Koski joins the orchestra for Mozart's beloved Piano Concerto No. 23, intimate, lyrical, and graceful before the evening closes with Maestro Nurhan Arman's own orchestral arrangement of Dvorak's glorious "American" String Quartet, one of the most joyful works in the chamber repertoire.

title.en: Rebellion Talks: Mackenzie's Unlikely Montreal Allies

ai.en: A Rebellion Talks session at Colborne Lodge on the Lower Canadian rebellion and its links to the Rebellion of 1837 in Toronto.

events.description: Learn about the rebellion in Lower Canada (Québec) and its connection to the Rebellion of 1837 in Toronto. The rebellion in Toronto wasn't the only one. At the same time revolutionaries were taking up arms here, an even bigger rebellion was breaking out in Lower Canada. Meet the Lower Canadian rebels and learn about Mackenzie's relationship with them. Join the conversation at Colborne Lodge, the historic home in High Park named in honour of the governor those rebels in Québec were trying to overthrow. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Orchestra Toronto explores the meeting of tradition and innovation, featuring Amely Zhou on erhu and Razak Pirani on tabla. The concert opens with Reena Esmail?s Testament (from Vishwas), a work that blends Indian classical sensibilities with Western orchestral textures, exploring themes of memory, identity, and faith. Canadian composer Kevin Lau?s Between the Earth and Forever follows, a reflective and expansive piece that draws listeners into its meditative landscapes and delicate harmonies. The program concludes with Shostakovich?s Symphony No. 5 in D Minor, a masterwork of tension and resilience, whose dramatic contrasts and haunting motifs reflect the composer?s struggles under Soviet censorship while remaining a testament to human endurance and expressive power.

ai.en: The final Rebellion Talks session at Gibson House on the burning of David Gibson's home in 1837.

events.description: Return for the thrilling conclusion of the story behind the burning of David Gibson’s home. The original house was razed to the ground in revenge for the role Gibson played in the rebellion. This time, the story is approached from the other side, through the life of the soldier who lit the flame: James FitzGibbon. The series comes to a close by exploring his life and connections to some of the most dramatic stories of his time, from battlefields, duels and riots to a touching love story and a tragic end. From October 2026 to April 2027, historian Adam Bunch brings Toronto’s history to life in a series of talks exploring the Upper Canada Rebellion and its lasting impact on the city. From spies and taverns to political reform, rural rebels and the Patriot War, each talk reveals a different story connected to the museum where it takes place.

events.description: Legal Age 19+ (Valid Photo I.D Required)For Love of Grace s tightest album to date, even glossy at times, but not tight enough to dull its pulse. With wordless howls, nastily detuned riffs that bend into harmony, breakdowns, handclaps, and a chaotic choral break seemingly played on pennywhistles, For Love of Grace s fundamental curiosity and trust in their instincts. Produced and mixed by the band (Rnnenfelt, Dan Kjr Nielsen, Jakob Tvilling Pless, Johan S. Weith, and Casper Morilla Fernandez) and Nis Bysted, For Love of Grace s Plowing Into the Field of Love at the same studio; its no coincidence its the only time they have returned to a studio to cut a record. The band wanted to capture the same intense energy. The band leaned on their experiences and the thousands of hours on stages theyve shared since they were teenagers. The setup was as minimal as possible: making decisions live and not overthinking, patient full takes with minimal overdubs. The lyrics were written only a few weeks before entering the studio to prevent the overall picture from being too fragmented and to increase the sense of risk and urgency. For Love of Grace s both fun and as serious as ever, growing and glowing through love. There is no affectation or prescription to this recordno palette of curated influence or sought sound. It is the sum total of inspirations, shared openly in the name of playing and playings pleasures.

title.en: Hannaford Street Silver presents April in Brass

ai.en: Hannaford Street Silver Band's April in Brass at Jane Mallett Theatre in Toronto, closing its 2026-27 season with new Canadian music, with the solo hornist Catherine Turner.

events.description: The Hannaford Street Silver Band concludes its 2026-27 season with April in Brass, a spectacular afternoon celebrating brass virtuosity, new Canadian music, and the remarkable versatility of the brass ensemble. Taking centre stage is Catherine Turner, solo hornist with the Orchestre symphonique de Montréal, performing Richard Strauss's magnificent Horn Concerto No. 1. Written in 1882-83 when Strauss was still a teenager, the concerto has become one of the defining works of the horn repertoire. Its soaring melodies, brilliant fanfares, lyrical passages, and demanding virtuosity make it an ideal showcase for the extraordinary colours and expressive possibilities of the horn. Turner brings her experience as a leading orchestral horn player to this exciting collaboration with Hannaford, creating an opportunity to hear one of the great works of the horn repertoire in a distinctive brass-band setting.

events.description: Orchestra Toronto celebrates the vibrancy of nature and human emotion in this program. The concert opens with Alice Ho?s Jubilation of Spring, a bright and dynamic work that captures the energy, color, and renewal of the season through inventive orchestral textures. Elgar?s Cello Concerto in E Minor, featuring Cellist Lucia Ticho, follows, a deeply introspective and lyrical masterpiece that showcases Ticho?s expressive range while conveying themes of loss, reflection, and hope. The program concludes with Beethoven?s Symphony No. 6, ?Pastoral?, a work that evokes the tranquility and rhythms of the countryside, celebrating humanity?s connection to the natural world with warmth, charm, and compositional ingenuity.

title.en: Music Toronto - Karen Ouzounian and Lembit Beecher's MAYRIG/MOTHER

ai.en: MAYRIG/MOTHER, by cellist Karen Ouzounian and composer-pianist Lembit Beecher, at the Jane Mallett Theatre for Music Toronto.

events.description: Cellist Karen Ouzounian, acclaimed for her work with the Silkroad Ensemble and the Aizuri Quartet, joins composer-pianist Lembit Beecher to close the season’s MUSE series with Mayrig, an immersive multimedia program centered on the human voice. Voices of Ouzounian’s mother and grandmother weave through Armenian music from Anatolia, songs of Lebanon, and the music of Charles Aznavour, alongside new works exploring memory, heritage, and resilience across generations. The program spans centuries and cultures, opening and closing with Marin Marais’s Les Voix Humaines. Traditional Armenian songs and early Anatolian recordings appear alongside arrangements of music by Charles Aznavour and Ashot Satyan. Original works by Lembit Beecher are joined by contemporary voices including Layale Chaker, Nathalie Joachim, Niloufar Nourbakhsh, and Karen Ouzounian, interwoven with recorded voices from Ouzounian’s family.

events.description: Known for his candid, emotionally resonant songwriting, Donovan Woods blends folk, country, and pop. In 2026, he is back with brand new music with his new EP, Squander Your Gifts. events.description: Written and Performed by Jake Epstein Directed by and developed with Robert McQueen Orchestrations, Arrangements and Musical Supervision by Daniel Abrahamson Best known as "that guy from Degrassi," Jake Epstein went on to star in the U.S. National Tours of Spring Awakening and American Idiot, play Spider-Man on Broadway, and originate the role of Gerry Goffin in Beautiful: The Carole King Musical. Not bad for a kid who once dreamed of Broadway from the back seat of his parents' minivan. In this newly updated version of his hit autobiographical musical, Boy Falls From the Sky, Epstein pulls back the curtain with humour and heart. Through unforgettable songs and candid stories - from touring the U.S. to surviving Spider-Man, from Broadway boos to backstage heartbreak - he reveals the rejection, fear, and resilience behind the spotlight. A funny, moving, and deeply human showbiz tell-all, Boy Falls From the Sky is for anyone who's ever dared to chase a dream.

title.en: Gennady Khazanov: On The Waves Of My Memory

events.description: An intimate evening with legendary actor and comedian Gennady Khazanov in ?On the Waves of My Memory? - filled with humor, personal stories, memories, and reflections on life and time. For more than half a century, Gennady Khazanov has been one of the most recognized and beloved figures of the stage. His unmistakable voice, brilliant sense of humor, sharp observations, and unique ability to make audiences laugh and think have made his performances unforgettable for generations. In ?On the Waves of My Memory,? Khazanov invites the audience into a personal conversation. He recalls remarkable people and encounters, shares stories rarely heard before, reflects on different eras and the passage of time, and revisits some of the classic pieces audiences know and love. This is more than a collection of famous monologues. It is a personal journey through memories, people, and moments that shaped an era ? told with Khazanov?s characteristic intelligence, irony, warmth, and humor.
